text.p: United States-based shopping mall operator Westfield America Trust said on Tuesday that its calendar 1996 net profit of A$26.61 million was slightly above the forecast of A$25.73 million in its prospectus issued ahead of the July 1996 float.

The company, whose assets were formerly owned by affiliate Wesfield Holdings Ltd, also said it achieved the prospectus forecast on all other key measures such as the cash distribution to unitholders of 4.24 cents per unit.
Barring unforeseen circumstances, the 1997 distribution was expected to be in line with forecast, directors said.
The trust, whose sole investment is in mall operator CenterMark Properties Inc, said CentreMark achieved property income of A$91.47 million compared with the prospectus forecast of A$91.03 million.
The Los Angeles-based executive director of Westfield America Management Ltd, Peter Lowy, said the result reflected the underlying strength and quality of CenterMark's 22 shopping centres.
Westfield America acquired a 53.3 percent interest in CenterMark in June 1996 and increased this to 67.2 percent in January 1997. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
